newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Canadian navy stops ships over U.N. Iraq sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Canadian navy stops ships over U.N. Iraq sanctions.

text.p: A Canadian frigate intercepted a merchant ship and wooden dhow in the Gulf at the weekend on suspicion of breaking United Nations sanctions against Iraq, a Canadian naval officer said on Tuesday.
Commander Tyrone Pile said his vessel Regina intercepted Qabas 2, an offshore replenishment vessel, on Saturday on suspicion it was carrying 450 tonnes of Iraqi fuel oil.
"All of the evidence found on the merchant ship led officials to believe that the Qabas 2 was in violation of U.N. trade embargo sanctions," the Canadian navy said in a statement earlier.
Pile told a news conference his vessel stopped a traditional wooden dhow al-Hamid the next day on suspicion of carrying 23 tonnes of fuel oil.
The dhow and its Indian crew, whose number he did not give, were being held in international waters awaiting entry to a regional port.
The Canadian frigate is part of a multinational force that checks shipping in the Gulf to enforce U.N. sanctions against Iraq imposed afer its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Since 1990 vessels from 14 countries have contributed ships to the force, which has intercepted more than 22,000 merchant ships and diverted more than 500 for carrying contraband cargo or inaccurate documents.
Pile spoke of "tension" caused by Iranian naval patrols, which he said monitored Western warships in the Gulf.
"It creates tension...tension of the unexpected," he said of Iranian patrol vessels sailing to within 1,000 metres (yards) of Western vessels to video tape them.
